built_from: warm-up material only (PR #36, #38, #43/#44); no final-benchmark proof
schema: fields follow the team Strategy Bank proposal (2026-11-02)

strategies.title: Split along the unfolded definition
strategies.description: Instead of induction on the variable followed by unfolding, split along the definition the statement applies to it.
strategies.when_to_apply: The original does `induction x`, then unfolds or simps `f`, and the statement applies `f` to `x`.
application_guide: Try `fun_induction f ...` (or the definition's own induction principle).
Close the generated branches with the cheapest step that works.
Compile one complete candidate before polishing.
risk_notes: The functional induction principle may not exist for every definition or version.
origin: PR #38 pattern 'split_by_def' (warm-up originals vs final submitted proofs)

strategies.title: Prove without induction
strategies.description: Build the goal directly from lemmas about the predicates and functions in the statement.
strategies.when_to_apply: The proof is mainly case branches produced by an induction or case split.
application_guide: Look for lemmas in the context that already relate the statement's functions.
Write one refine/exact/rw chain.
risk_notes: May not exist; keep the split route as fallback.

strategies.title: Merge branches that end the same way
strategies.description: Close branches with the same ending once, with `<;>`, `all_goals` or `first | .. | ..`, and close simple branches directly.
strategies.when_to_apply: Many case branches, several ending with the same steps, or simple branches closed by constructors or hypotheses.
application_guide: Find branches whose final steps coincide.
Apply one combinator after the split; close trivial branches with `exact`/`assumption`.
risk_notes: Uniform automation over all branches can raise heartbeats sharply.
origin: PR #38 pattern 'combinator' (warm-up originals vs final submitted proofs)
PR #44 passes.md row 'branches closed by constructors and hypotheses' (warm-up edits, PR #43)

strategies.title: Inline one-use intermediate claims
strategies.description: Remove or inline `have` steps that are used once; pass facts directly as arguments.
application_guide: Check each `have` is used at most once.
Inline it at the use site or rewrite the goal with it.
Keep every claim a later step needs.
risk_notes: Inlining can duplicate work if the claim is used more than once.
origin: PR #38 pattern 'have_chain' (warm-up originals vs final submitted proofs)
PR #44 passes.md row 'one-use intermediate hypothesis' (warm-up edits, PR #43)

strategies.title: Prove a shared part once
strategies.description: Prove one general statement for near-duplicate parts inside the proof and reuse it.
application_guide: Identify the common shape of the repeated blocks.
State it once with `have key : ∀ ...` and apply it.
risk_notes: The general statement may cost more than the copies it replaces.
origin: PR #44 passes.md row 'same condition proved in several places' (warm-up edits, PR #43)

strategies.title: Localize broad automation
strategies.description: Replace repeated broad automation by narrowly targeted calls.
strategies.when_to_apply: The same closer (simp_all, grind, aesop, linarith, ...) is used many times.
application_guide: Pick the most expensive automation site.
Use `simp only [..]`, a single targeted lemma or a cheaper closer there.
Do not run `simp_all` over all hypotheses.
risk_notes: A focused replacement is not guaranteed to lower heartbeats.
origin: PR #38 pattern 'automation' (warm-up originals vs final submitted proofs)
PR #44 passes.md row 'broad automation or repeated alternatives' (warm-up edits, PR #43)

strategies.title: Give the exact witness instead of searching
strategies.description: Where the proof searches (decide, long normalisation, numeric case checks), give the exact witness, bound or library equation.
application_guide: Find the search step.
Replace it with the explicit term or library equation.
risk_notes: The explicit term can be longer in tokens.
origin: PR #38 pattern 'exact_form' (warm-up originals vs final submitted proofs)

strategies.title: Extract with obtain and rebuild with constructors
strategies.description: Replace nested `.elim` and lambdas by `obtain` and constructors applied in order.
strategies.when_to_apply: Long proof terms with `.elim` or several `fun` binders.
application_guide: Extract the needed hypotheses with `obtain`.
Apply the goal's constructors in order.
risk_notes: Binder scope and existential witnesses must stay the same.
origin: PR #44 passes.md row 'nested .elim / lambdas / long proof terms' (warm-up edits, PR #43)

strategies.title: Trim simp lists
strategies.description: Drop unused simp lemmas and narrow the simp scope.
application_guide: Remove lemmas one at a time and recompile.
Compare `simp only` with the short form.
risk_notes: The simp set can behave differently across versions.
origin: PR #44 passes.md row 'simp lists or repeated simplification' (warm-up edits, PR #43)

strategies.title: Reuse an existing theorem
strategies.description: Replace whole parts of the argument with an existing theorem from the context or library.
strategies.when_to_apply: Always applicable as a general move.
application_guide: Search the context and library for a lemma that states a large part of the goal.
Apply it instead of re-proving its content.
risk_notes: The lemma must exist in every required version.
origin: PR #38 pattern 'reuse' (warm-up originals vs final submitted proofs)

strategies.title: Rebuild the route when local edits stall
strategies.description: When small edits stop improving, rebuild the whole proof route in a separate candidate.
strategies.when_to_apply: General move after repeated non-improving candidates.
application_guide: Keep the best proof.
Write a new route from an existing lemma in a separate candidate.
risk_notes: Costs budget; use after local edits stall.
origin: PR #44 passes.md row 'large duplicated structure or stalled local edits' (warm-up edits, PR #43)
